# repo-setup — the opencharly org, dotgithub config, and new-repo setup

This skill is the companion to `/charly-internals:git-workflow`: git-workflow
owns the AUTHOR's branch/PR discipline; repo-setup owns the ORG-LEVEL
configuration that discipline relies on and the checklist for standing up a
NEW repository.

## The org model (verified against the live settings)

- The `opencharly` org is on GitHub **Team**, so org **rulesets** and the
  `workflows` rule ("Require workflows to pass") are available.
- ONE organization branch ruleset named
  `org-wide required workflow & main protection` is the single source of main
  protection and the required workflow. It targets `~ALL` repositories MINUS an
  explicit exclude set, on `refs/heads/main`, and carries:
  * `workflows` — requires
    `opencharly/.github/.github/workflows/org-wide-pr-validator-required.yml@refs/heads/main`
    (read from the `.github` repo at the pinned ref);
  * `required_status_checks` — `strict: true`, exactly ONE context
    `validate / validate`;
  * `non_fast_forward`, `deletion`, `creation`.
  The ONLY bypass actor is the `charly-auto-merge` GitHub App (its protected-main
  CHANGELOG writes must land). There is NO human bypass and NO `pull_request`
  review rule — the validator IS the gate.
- Owner script: `opencharly/.github/scripts/org-ruleset.sh` (`apply` / `verify`).
  It builds **two** org rulesets from ONE payload builder — A for the active
  non-fork `main`-default repos, B for the active **forks** on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` —
  deletes redundant per-repo rulesets and any surviving legacy branch protection,
  and enforces the settings that have NO org-level default: `allow_auto_merge=true`,
  `delete_branch_on_merge=true`, and `allow_update_branch=false`.
- The sets are `discover_repos` (**active, non-fork, default `main`**) and
  `discover_forks` (active forks, with their default branch). Ruleset A targets the
  first on `refs/heads/main`; ruleset B targets the second on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` —
  `stable`/`master` included — with the **same rules, including the `workflows`
  rule**. So a fork's `validate / validate` is produced by the ORG required workflow
  and **no per-fork `pr-validator.yml` is copied into a fork**. The gate cannot be
  switched off by deleting a fork file.
- A first-party fork is therefore a LANDING TARGET like any other. The one file it
  carries is `.github/workflows/tag-on-merge.yml`, installed and kept canonical by
  `reconcile-tag-on-merge-callers.sh` with `SCOPE=forks` — which also INSTALLS it
  where absent. A fork left out of ruleset B fails `org-ruleset.sh verify` by name
  until the next `apply` (the staleness control).
- A fork's `workflows` rule blocks DIRECT pushes, so a user-token `gh repo sync`
  fails (measured, opencharly/.github#179). Sync through
  `.github/workflows/sync-forks.yml`, which uses the `charly-auto-merge` App token —
  the ruleset bypass actor. It never forces; a conflict is reported.
- Still outside the gate: an archived repo, a vendored upstream on a non-`main`
  default (`pixelflux` → `av1`), and an artifact-branch sink
  (`omarchy-eval-artifacts` → `runs`).

## What happens automatically on every PR (the landing chain)

1. A PR is opened/updated → the org ruleset runs
   `org-wide-pr-validator-required.yml` in the TARGET repo's context (definition
   from `opencharly/.github` at the pinned ref) → it calls the reusable
   `pr-validator.yml` → the single required check `validate / validate`.
2. On a PASS verdict the validator enables GitHub **native auto-merge (squash)**
   inline — there is NO separate auto-merge workflow. `main` is squash-only.
3. After the merge, the PER-REPO caller `.github/workflows/tag-on-merge.yml`
   fires (on `workflow_run` of `charly/pr-validator` + `push` to main) → calls the
   org reusable `tag-on-merge.yml`, which mints the CalVer tag
   `v<YYYY>.<DDD>.<HHMM>` at the merge commit and writes `CHANGELOG/<CalVer>.md`
   from the merged PR body (the body IS the changelog). Proxy-consumed root
   modules (`sdk`, `spec`, `plugin-gh`) get the Go-module `v0.<YYYYDDD>.<HHMM>`
   form instead.

   **A landing in one of those repos is not tagged at the merge instant.** The org sweep that mints the tag
   runs on `workflow_run` of `charly/pr-validator` and scans the last 24h of merged PRs, so a native-auto-merge
   squash - which GitHub Actions creates ZERO runs for - is tagged when the NEXT validator completes in that
   repo, not when it merges. Measured and diagnosed on `sdk`'s own `.github/workflows/tag-on-merge.yml`, whose
   header RCA states it: do not read a missing tag minutes after a merge in `sdk`, `spec` or `plugin-gh` as a
   defect.
4. A body-only fix after the head was pushed needs NO empty commit: re-run the
   failed run MANUALLY with `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<run-id>/rerun`
   (not `gh run rerun`, which 404s on the org-required workflow; the re-run's newer
   check run supersedes the failure). The org-wide `rerun` label sweep was RETIRED.

## Step 0 — choose the class and the name (do this BEFORE step 1)

The repo name is not a free choice: it carries the **class**, and the class
decides what the repo may hold. Settle the class first, then the name, then run
the checklist below.

1. **What is the entity?** A candy or image, a VM, a plugin, a service bundle, a
   packaging repo, a distro family, or a whole product family — the KIND axis.
2. **Which family does it belong to** (`openclaw`, `selkies`, `agentteams`, …)?
   The family word is also the skill namespace (`/charly-<family>:<skill>`) and
   the corpus directory.
3. **Which repo owns it?** One canonical owner per behaviour (the rulebook's R2);
   every other repo *references* it by `@github.com/<owner>/<repo>:<vX.Y.Z>` or a
   namespace import.
4. **Name it by its class.** Bare names are for core/contract (`charly`, `sdk`,
   `spec`, `marketplace`, `docs`) and appliances **only**. Everything else carries
   its prefix — `distro-`, `charly-`/`pkg-`, `layer-`, `plugin-`, `pod-`, `vm-` —
   and a **product family is a `layer-<family>` repo** (`layer-agentteams` is the
   canonical example, `layer-openclaw` follows it). A family is never a bare name.

The full class → name → "may hold" mapping is the umbrella `README.md`
("The org map"), verified by `charly task org-map`; the rule itself
is in the umbrella `AGENTS.md` ("Repo classes and naming"). Do not copy either
table into this skill: they are the canonical surfaces, and a copy drifts.

**A repo whose only content is skills is not a class.** No prefix exists for it, and
none may be invented. A `layer-*`, `distro-*`, `plugin-*`, `pod-*`, `vm-*`, `charly-*` or
`pkg-*` repo must hold the code, plugin or config its name promises, with its skills
beside that content (umbrella `AGENTS.md` Part II #5). A `*-skills` carrier REPO that
exists only to own prose is retired by this rule. Its skills move to the repo of the
entity they describe, or to the umbrella when they are general guidance. A carrier
CANDY inside a repo that already holds code is a different thing and is unaffected:
it is the shape image-owned skills need (`/charly-internals:skills`).

Worked counter-example, because it happened: a product family was created as a
bare `openclaw`. It held a box, a candy, a disposable bed and two skills — a
`layer-<family>` shape — so the name did not fit its class and the repo was
renamed to `layer-openclaw`. A bare name holding anything beyond core/contract or
an appliance is the defect this step exists to catch.

## Setting up a NEW repository (checklist)

The org ruleset's **`creation`** rule makes the naive path IMPOSSIBLE, and it is the first step every
new repo gets wrong: a repo's first `main` cannot be created by `git push`, by the contents API, by
`repo auto_init`, or by a branch rename — each fails with *"Cannot create ref due to creations being
restricted"* (and `auto_init` leaves the repo with no refs at all). The only actor that can create that
ref is the `charly-auto-merge` App, and the org ships a workflow that mints exactly that token for this
purpose. So the order is:

1. **Create the repo EMPTY and non-fork** — `gh repo create opencharly/<name> --public`, with **no**
   `--add-readme`, `--gitignore`, license or `auto_init` (blocked anyway; see above). Adopting an
   existing upstream is an explicit choice: NON-FORK (it gains the org gate and CalVer tags) or a fork
   (it lands on its own CI, as `openclaw-enterprise` does, or on its own repo-scoped ruleset, as
   `crabbox` does, and the org mints no tag for it).
2. **Push ONE throwaway seed branch.** Creating any ref that is not `main` is allowed:
   `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/seed`. The seed must carry **no content you will ship** — `main` is
   created at it, and a PR whose diff is empty is a no-op.
3. **Bootstrap `main` with the org workflow**:
   `gh workflow run bootstrap-repo-main.yml --repo opencharly/.github -f repos=<name>`. It mints the
   App token, creates `refs/heads/main` at the seed, and **INSTALLS and asserts the per-repo
   `.github/workflows/tag-on-merge.yml` caller** — so do NOT hand-add that file. The installed caller
   IS the canonical `tag-on-merge-dispatcher.yml`; a committed copy differs by a byte (no final
   newline) and fights every future template regeneration.
4. **Set the three repository settings the App cannot** (it holds no `administration` permission):

   ```sh
   gh api --method PATCH repos/opencharly/<name> \
     -f default_branch=main -f allow_auto_merge=true -f delete_branch_on_merge=true
   ```

   Until this runs the repo is **outside the org gate**: no required `validate / validate`, no CalVer
   tag, no CHANGELOG (`org-ruleset.sh verify` reports it as `needs_operator_settings=<n>`). Do NOT
   re-apply the org ruleset on its behalf — the ONE ruleset targets `~ALL` minus an explicit exclude
   set, so a new repo is already covered; only these three settings have no org-level default.
5. **Land the content as ONE PR off `main`** (never a direct push): a `feat/` branch, the commit, the
   change-class gate on that tree, the whole body, one push, a ready PR. Because step 3 installed the
   caller, the FIRST merge is tagged.
6. **In the umbrella**, the gitlink and the pin's INTENT land in the SAME commit. `git submodule add
   <url> <path>` writes **no** `branch =`, and a path with neither an `intent:` entry nor a `branch=`
   is `unpinned` — which fails `charly task verify` **structurally**:

   ```sh
   git submodule add <url> <path>
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<path>.branch main     # the pin's INTENT (a leaf)
   ```

   then the `import:` key (if the repo has entities to address), the README org-map row and the counts
   that reconciler checks. The mechanism and the why are `/charly-internals:git-workflow`
   (its pin-intent-and-currency reference, "A submodule is BORN `unpinned`"); this checklist repeats
   the two commands because a checklist is read on its own, and cites the owner of the rule rather than
   restating the reasoning. Advance THIS pin with the narrow mechanism, NOT with `charly task sync`:
   that verb is an ORG-WIDE wave (Part II #3), it advances every pin the umbrella declares, and it
   holds the worktree's index while it runs.
7. **Verify the org issue labels** (this is the whole label contract for a new repo):

   a. **`opencharly/.github` owns everything label-related** — the taxonomy
      (`labels/taxonomy.json`), the generic rules (`labels/category-rules.json`), the org issue
      form (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.yml`, the default community-health file), the
      sync/audit workflows and the tests. **A repository ships no label configuration of its
      own, ever.**
   b. **The bootstrap sync provisions the labels.** `bootstrap-repo-main.yml` runs
      `scripts/labels.sh sync --repo <name>`; the 12 labels (`category:runtime`,
      `category:delivery`, `category:verification`, `category:experience`,
      `category:governance`, `category:hygiene`; `type:fix`, `type:feat`, `type:design`,
      `type:spec`, `type:docs`, `type:chore`) exist in every non-archived repo. Verify them:
      `gh label list -R opencharly/<name> --limit 100 | grep -E '^(category|type):'` must show
      all 12; if the sync has not run, run `gh workflow run label-sync.yml --repo
      opencharly/.github -f repos=<name>`.
   c. **Do not ship a repository-specific issue template** unless it carries the same four
      required fields as the org form — Category, Type, Remedy / files the remedy will touch,
      and Cited design decision or org-rulebook rule (or `none`). A repo template **overrides**
      the org default (a GitHub limitation), so a template without those fields silently breaks
      mandatory labelling for that repo. The safest choice is no template at all.
   d. **No repository-specific label.** Labels are fully generic: the repository name is never
      a classification signal, every category is available in every repo, and a new or future
      repo needs no mapping. A label like `session:`, `owner:`, `priority:`, `severity:`,
      `size:`, `status:` or any repo/product-named label is a defect the audit reports.
   e. **File through the org form or `scripts/gh/cli.ts issue`**, which refuses without
      `category:`, `type:`, remedy/files, the cited rule, the verified RCA and a
      `--blocking`/`--non-blocking` classification — never a bare `gh issue create`.
      The full "which label" rules, the split protocol and the DESIGN/rulebook violation table
      are in `/charly-internals:git-workflow`, under its issue-labels reference page.
   f. **Expect the org `label-audit` to check the new repo** daily: it reports missing axes,
      two values on one axis, retired/default labels and unknown labels (report-only by
      default); `label-sync` re-provisions the 12 labels because GitHub recreates its 9
      defaults on every new repository.

### Onboarding a fork

1. **Do not add a repo-scoped ruleset and do not add a `pr-validator.yml`.** Run
   `scripts/org-ruleset.sh apply`; ruleset B picks the fork up from
   `discover_forks`. A fork missing from B fails `verify` until apply runs — that is
   the staleness control, not a warning.
2. **Install the tag-on-merge caller**: dispatch
   `.github/workflows/reconcile-tag-on-merge-callers.yml` with `scope=forks`. An
   absent caller is INSTALLED there (the targets scope never installs); a copy that
   pins the reusable to a SHA keeps that policy with the current `.github` main sha.
3. **Confirm the settings** `org-ruleset.sh apply` asserts (`allow_auto_merge`,
   `delete_branch_on_merge`, `allow_update_branch=false`). With auto-merge disabled,
   an approved PR renders as a FAILED check (opencharly/.github#212).
4. **Land one canary PR.** Confirm exactly ONE `validate / validate` run on the head
   (two is a duplicate producer — stop), native squash auto-merge armed, the merge,
   and a CalVer tag plus `CHANGELOG/<CalVer>.md` on the fork's DEFAULT branch.
5. **Sync from upstream with `sync-forks.yml`**, never a user-token `gh repo sync`
   (the `workflows` rule blocks a direct push).
6. **Tag-on-merge means the fork mints CalVer**: a pin at the caller-install commit
   is `pre-release-process`, above it `changelog-tip` or `tagged` (DESIGN A.12).

## The measured gap this checklist prevents

A repo created WITHOUT the `tag-on-merge.yml` caller still MERGES (the org
workflow validates it) but NEVER gets a CalVer tag: measured on
`layer-nerdctl` and `plugin-nerdctl` (no `.github` directory at all; their two
`v2026.266.*` tags were minted manually).

Three DIFFERENT things sit outside the gate, and they are not one category:

- **A vendored upstream on a non-`main` default** — `pixelflux` (default
  `av1`): consumed as a pin, not a landing target.
- **An artifact-branch sink** — `omarchy-eval-artifacts` (default `runs`): a
  branch that receives published output, not a landing target.
- **An archived repo** — `pi-review-action`: read-only, so GitHub rejects
  pushes and new PRs. `org-ruleset.sh verify` names any archived fork too.

A first-party FORK is no longer in this set: ruleset B gates it, and it mints
CalVer once its tag-on-merge caller is installed. The org mints no AUTOMATIC tag
for a repo with no caller, so a CalVer tag you find there was minted out-of-band.

Invoke when creating or onboarding a repository in the opencharly org, when adding
or changing CI/landing workflows, or when explaining what the org ruleset and
dotgithub workflows do automatically versus what each repo must configure.
